routes.label: Apply both factors to the area

question: When the base of a triangle is increased \(10\%\) and the altitude to this base is decreased \(10\%,\) the change in area is:
solution:
Let the original base and corresponding altitude be \(b,h>0\), so the original area is \(K=\tfrac12bh\). Increasing the base by \(10\%\) multiplies it by \(1.10\), while decreasing the altitude by \(10\%\) multiplies it by \(0.90\). The new area is therefore
\[
\frac12(1.10b)(0.90h)
=0.99\left(\frac12bh\right)
=0.99K.
\]
The area becomes \(99\%\) of its original value, a \(\boxed{1\%\text{ decrease}}\), choice \(\mathrm E\).
